item.title: Taxi drivers rarely die of Alzheimer's
item.description:
📝 But that study on taxi and ambulance drivers made me wonder whether all that mental work might be doing something good to the brain. The researchers found that London taxi drivers had measurably more gray matter in the posterior hippocampus, a brain area tied to storing large-scale spatial maps. That volume tracked with experience: The longer someone had driven, the larger that part of the brain.
🔗 Read more: https://theconversation.com/taxi-drivers-rarely-die-of-alzheimers-how-complex-mental-maps-and-spatial-reasoning-protect-your-brain-286650

Show HN: Today's cities on a globe of Earth's tectonic past and future
item.description:
📝 Country polygons are split by the present-day static polygons from the Merdith 2021 plate model, then each country-on-plate fragment is reconstructed backward with pyGPlates finite rotations. The future side is a constant-motion extrapolation from young plate rotations with a few coarse collision handoffs, so treat it as an interactive sketch rather than a forecast. Red areas mark plate fragments that still overlap after reconstruction.
🔗 Read more: https://douwe.com/projects/tectonic_globe
